evals.prompt: Our new matching agent resolved 88 of 110 assigned ledger batches versus 84 for the old version. It ran on a different month and only successful batches have item-level validation. Design an evaluation we can run without changing production.
evals.expected_output: Use a matched snapshot, compare final records against reconciliation invariants, include all assigned batches, report missing validation and costs, and decline a causal or release claim based on unmatched months. No interactive chat or human scoring is required.

evals.prompt: A proposed retrieval change makes help-desk answers faster. We have a held-out set of questions with policy revisions, feedback from users of only the current version, and an isolated replay service. Decide what we can learn before rollout.
evals.expected_output: Replay matched questions against the same policy revision, independently check correctness and citations, stratify regressions, and measure latency alongside task success. Label effects on live users unmeasured and specify a comparable, bounded trial.

evals.prompt: We changed the shared model for a travel agent. Our replay sends the recorded follow-up 'yes' to both versions. The baseline asked whether to hold the fare. The candidate asked whether to buy it. Its score rose two points with a newly edited judge. How much confidence should we have?
evals.expected_output: Identify the invalid follow-up and changed grading instrument. Restore the same pre-decision state, evaluate the first answer or branch with a pinned simulator, and keep future history hidden. Regrade both arms under one validated rubric, use baseline repeats to estimate noise, and cover other workflows affected by the shared default. Require independent evidence for purchase authorization. Treat the current lift as inconclusive.

evals.prompt: A new optional glossary feature adds plain-language definitions to technical reports. The existing suite checks spelling only. A proposed judge agreed with the editor on all 12 definitions used to write its rubric. Can we use it as the launch gate?
evals.expected_output: Design a focused capability check for accurate, useful definitions and retain relevant regressions. Test the grader on separate domain-labeled examples, including fluent but incorrect definitions. Report coverage, consequential disagreements and evidence needed before using it as a gate. Avoid claiming held-out agreement from rubric-development examples.
